references.text: By the word of the Lord were the heavens made, all their host by the breath of his mouth.
For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood firm.
The day is yours, and the night also is yours; you have set up the light and the sun.
He wraps himself in light as with a garment; he stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain.
I form the light and create darkness, I bring prosperity and create disaster. I, the Lord, do all these things.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. ... In him was life, and that life was the light of all mankind. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
For God, who said, 'Let light shine out of darkness,' made his light shine in our hearts to give us the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God's command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible.
And this is the message we have heard from him and declare to you: God is light; in him there is no darkness at all.
Both illustrate God's creative word as immediately bringing about reality.
Uses the creation motif of light from darkness as a metaphor for spiritual resurrection.
A prophetic call to become light, built upon the light of creation as God's glory.
An ironic contrast: false light (Baal) is summoned in opposition to God's true light.
